messages:
marco: Quick update: stratus-lowlat-v1 is GA on Hosted API. Its tuned for sub-50ms p99 token latency for short-turns and includes streaming + tool-calling support. Docs + migration: https://docs.redwood.ai/hosted/stratus-lowlat.
rachel: awesome — does this change any default rate limits or quotas for Hosted users?
marco: No quota changes today. Were introducing an optional latency-tier flag on routes: latency_tier: low | standard. low maps to the low-latency execution path and will prefer small-batch, high-priority scheduling. Billing same as hosted token pricing for now.
casey: infra note: low-latency nodes use a different allocator and are pinned to GPUs with high-clock cores. This means slightly reduced throughput per GPU; autoscale config may need adjustment if you have high concurrency long sessions.
marco: rollout plan: canary 5% 1792104800 (48h monitor), then 25% 7d window, full after 14 days assuming no regressions. Hosted orgs will be auto-assigned to standard unless they opt into low tier. Opt-in via org settings or route override.
rachel: sample streaming snippet with tool-calls?
marco: ```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{"model":"stratus-lowlat-v1","input":"Extract actions","enable_tool_calls":true}'
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/realtime/stream
```
casey: ops checklist: update internal LB health checks to accept 102/3 handshake for chunked streams, and make sure SDKs honor the new X-Redwood-Latency-Tier header. SDK PRs ready in infra/clients.
docs-bot: Migration guide published: https://docs.redwood.ai/hosted/stratus-lowlat#migration (includes benchmarks, curl/SDK examples, and recommended smoke tests).
marco: If you maintain customer integrations that pin to model names, please test with small prompt sets and report anomalies in #incidents. Were watching latency, error-rate, and token regressions.
rachel: noted, will coordinate smoke runs. congrats team! :tada:
